section_summary: This section documents United States policy debates and economic analyses regarding occupied Japan during the summer and early autumn of 1947. Key topics include disputes between the State Department, the War Department, and the Far Eastern Commission over SWNCC 380 and the unilateral issuance of interim directives on Japanese reparations and industrial levels. The section also features a comprehensive SCAP report on severe inflation, food rationing, and industrial stagnation under the Katayama Cabinet, as well as high-level planning to utilize Japanese gold and silver reserves to establish the Occupied Japan Export-Import Revolving Fund.

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum setting forth objections to SWNCC 380 regarding unilateral interim directives for Japanese economic policies.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring recommends disapproving SWNCC 380, arguing against notifying the Far Eastern Commission of unilateral US deadline dates for action.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on SWNCC 380, Unilateral Action on Japanese Economic Problems

subfiles.about: Division of Japanese Affairs memorandum agreeing that a separate policy paper on SWNCC 380 is unnecessary.
subfiles.summary: Borton agrees with Penfield, suggesting SWNCC papers include target completion dates and consider interim directives if FEC action stalls.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum on SWNCC 380
subfiles.to: James K. Penfield and Edwin M. Martin

subfiles.about: Office of Far Eastern Affairs memorandum opposing the adoption of SWNCC 380 as a formal policy paper.
subfiles.summary: Penfield advises against imposing rigid deadlines on the Far Eastern Commission, arguing that a formal policy paper is unnecessary.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum on SWNCC 380

subfiles.about: Letter advising against issuing an interim directive to SCAP establishing the level of economic life in Japan.
subfiles.summary: McCoy argues that issuing a unilateral directive on FEC-218 would disrupt Commission negotiations and violate international cooperation without urgency.
subfiles.title: Letter from General Frank R. McCoy to General John H. Hilldring on the Level of Economic Life in Japan

subfiles.about: Draft reply concurring with General McCoy that no interim directive on Japanese economic levels should be issued.
subfiles.summary: Draft letter informing McCoy that State and War Departments agreed not to issue an interim directive on FEC-218.
subfiles.title: Draft Letter from Charles E. Saltzman to General Frank R. McCoy

subfiles.about: Official notification that the State and War Departments will not issue an interim directive on FEC-218.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman confirms agreement with Secretary Royall that no interim directive will be issued on the level of economic life.
subfiles.title: Letter from Charles E. Saltzman to General Frank R. McCoy

subfiles.about: Detailed critique of SWNCC 380 and the War Department's proposal for unilateral interim directives.
subfiles.summary: McCoy defends the Far Eastern Commission's record, attributing past policy delays primarily to US administrative processes rather than allied obstructionism.
subfiles.title: Letter from General Frank R. McCoy to General John H. Hilldring on SWNCC 380

subfiles.about: Misplaced page 21 of the SCAP report analyzing urban food rationing, harvest estimates, and Tokyo black market prices.
subfiles.from: Research and Statistics Division, Economic and Scientific Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: Report fragment examining delayed Tokyo staple rations, summer grain harvest increases, and rising black market food prices following elections.
subfiles.title: Report Fragment on Food Supply and Prices in Japan

subfiles.about: Inquiry from The Utah Construction Company regarding contracting opportunities for American engineering firms in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Keller inquires whether American construction firms may participate in anticipated Japanese rehabilitation projects, citing company experience in the Philippines.
subfiles.title: Letter from F. M. Keller to Edwin M. Martin Regarding Construction Work in Japan

subfiles.about: State Department response explaining limited prospects for American engineering firms in occupied Japan.
subfiles.summary: Whitman explains that US occupation funding is restricted to basic food and raw materials rather than American contracting firms.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to F. M. Keller Regarding Construction Work in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmittal despatch forwarding five copies of the SCAP Economic and Scientific Section report on economic conditions in Japan.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.summary: Despatch transmitting the SCAP economic report and referencing previous Japanese Government economic policy statements.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1233: Report Entitled 'Economic Conditions in Japan'

subfiles.about: Comprehensive SCAP report evaluating Japanese industrial production, foreign trade, inflation, price-wage policies, and fiscal deficits.
subfiles.from: Research and Statistics Division, Economic and Scientific Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: This comprehensive report analyzes severe structural bottlenecks impeding Japanese economic recovery as of August 1947. Industrial output stands at only 41 percent of pre-war levels due to critical shortages of coal, imported raw materials, and electrical power. Acute inflation and black market distribution continue to depress real wages, forcing the Katayama Cabinet to implement comprehensive price controls and fiscal subsidies.
subfiles.title: Economic Conditions in Japan

subfiles.about: Legal inquiry regarding the pledging and removal of Japanese gold and silver stocks to secure import loans.
subfiles.summary: Whitman requests a legal opinion on whether FEC policy allows pledging Japanese gold reserves as bank loan collateral.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum on Interpretation of Paragraph 16c, FEC-032/26

subfiles.about: Discussions with British Embassy and UK Treasury representatives regarding the revolving fund and petroleum refining capacity.
subfiles.summary: British officials concur with US interpretations permitting SCAP to pledge gold reserves, while discussing petroleum refining limits in FEC.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on Japanese Gold and Silver Revolving Fund and FEC Committee No. 2

subfiles.about: Inter-agency meeting regarding bank credit requirements and the potential transfer of Japanese gold reserves to North America.
subfiles.summary: Vallance summarizes discussions on pledging Japanese gold to secure cotton financing from the Export-Import Bank and private banks.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Transfer of Gold and Silver Reserves for Japanese Textile Credits

subfiles.about: Concluding page of SCAP circular detailing asset definitions, accounting rules, Controller reporting, and eventual fund liquidation.
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: Circular section specifying revolving fund asset definitions, Controller monthly reporting obligations, and eventual fund liquidation upon a peace treaty.
subfiles.title: SCAP Circular: Establishment of Occupied Japan Export-Import Revolving Fund (Page 3 Fragment)

subfiles.about: State Department recommendations on wording modifications for the SCAP circular establishing the Export-Import Revolving Fund.
subfiles.summary: Whitman proposes specific drafting changes regarding import withdrawals, minimum cash reserve ratios, and net worth calculations in the circular.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to Paul Cleveland on Export-Import Revolving Fund Circular

subfiles.about: First two pages of SCAP circular creating the revolving fund with $137 million in gold assets to finance trade.
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: Circular establishing the Occupied Japan Export-Import Revolving Fund, designating management authority, defining assets including gold, and outlining expenditure limitations.
subfiles.title: SCAP Circular: Establishment of Occupied Japan Export-Import Revolving Fund (Pages 1-2 Fragment)
